answer: Operator lien: each identity needs a real-world asset pledge recorded off-chain, and any cluster flagged by graph analysis freezes every pledge tied to that same operator. This turns an island of cheap wallets into a single collateral pool an attacker must overfund to keep operating. Enforcement traces registry records to the person, so a karst of hidden subsidiaries cannot dilute the penalty. The result: cloning costs the full pledged value per operator, not per wallet, draining the nectar of scale attacks.
